About Us
Meet our team
We’re a dynamic group of individuals who are passionate about what we do and dedicated to delivering the best results for our clients.
Veterinary Surgeons:
Rob Hamilton
Rob is one of our founders and qualified in 2001 from the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons, London. He has spent most of his professional time in small animal practice and has a special interest in laparoscopic & endoscopic procedures. Rob is passionate about all things 'keyhole' as has brought laparoscopic surgery to many practices across the UK. He has the general practitioner and post graduate certificates in small animal endoscopy and endosurgery. In his downtime he enjoys a game of golf or darts, tours the tennis courts of Britain with 3 of his tennis-playing children, and occasionally stays at home with his Sphynx cats.
Ryan Davis
Ryan is one of our co-founders and specialist surgeons. He graduated from the University of Glasgow in 2002 and has since completed a post-graduate certificate in surgery, is an RCVS advanced practitioner in surgery, and has an ILM Level 5 in Leadership and Management. He spends most of his time in theatre and especially enjoys fracture management and reconstructive skin surgery. On the days he isn’t at Southwater, he teaches surgery at many practices across the UK! Outside of work, he enjoys cooking and cars, and spending time with his naughty rescue terrier, Moose.
Naomi Brown
Naomi has been working at Southwater since we opened in 2023. She graduated from the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons, London, in 2015 and has since gained a qualification in small animal surgery. Her special interests include surgery (especially soft tissue), dentistry, and small animals. Outside of work, she enjoys running, baking, growing veg, and hiking with her Staffie Cross, Blue!
Catalin Demeter
Catalin graduated from University in Romania in 2010 and has been working at Southwater since we opened in 2023. He has since completed a CertAVP (Surgery) and a GPCert (Oncology) from the International School of Veterinary Post-graduate Sciences (ISVPS). At work, he is especially interested in surgery, oncological surgery, oncology, and diagnostics. Outside of work, he enjoys reading, nature walks, fishing, traditional ju-jitsu, and spending time with his rescue dogs, Mike and John, and 3 cats!
Lauren Turley
Lauren graduated from the Royal Veterinary College, London, in 2012 and joined the team at Southwater in 2024. She has a certificate in small animal surgery and an associate fellowship in higher education (as part of her teaching at Harper Keele Vet School). She enjoys all aspects of small animal practice, particularly orthopaedics. She has three dogs; Nellie the Border Terrier, River the Clumber Spaniel, and Roo the Cocker Spaniel. When she isn’t walking her crazy bunch, she trains for and competes in triathlons!
Carwyn Lee
Carwyn graduated from the University of Liverpool in 2019 and joined the SW team in 2025. He is currently completing a surgical certificate and is particularly interested in orthopaedics. Outside of work, he spends a lot of time in the countryside; fishing and walking his two lovely spaniels, Dylis and Fin. He also has two cats, Percy and Fish, who have both been rescued from work!
Rachel Howell
Rachel graduated from the University of Liverpool in 2010 and joined the team at Southwater in 2025. She completed a post-graduate certificate in small animal medicine and has held an RCVS advanced practitioner status in this area since 2016. As you can probably tell, she loves all things medicine! Outside of work, she spends most of her time looking after her two children, but she does find the time to attend a weekly ballet class!
Heidi Whieldon
Heidi is the newest vet in the SW team, having only started in 2026. She graduated from the University of Liverpool in 1998 and has since gained a post-graduate certificate and advanced practitioner status in small animal surgery. She has particular interests in soft tissue surgery and endoscopy. Outside of work, she can be found flying a four-seater plane, scuba diving, and spending time with her animals; Zara the black Labrador, Bert the tuxedo cat, and some chickens!
Registered Veterinary Nurses:
Joedie Evans
Joedie began her veterinary journey at just 14 years old and has dedicated her career to caring for animals and supporting the next generation of veterinary professionals. After qualifying as a Registered Veterinary Nurse in 2014, she became a Clinical Coach, mentoring student nurses, before going on to lecture in Animal Management and share her knowledge of animal care, welfare and nursing.
Joedie joined Southwater Veterinary Group in 2023 as Head RVN and leads a passionate nursing team of 11. She has a particular interest in anaesthesia, orthopaedic and soft tissue surgery, post-operative care and phlebotomy, and is proud to be part of such a supportive and compassionate team.
Outside of work, Joedie enjoys adventures with her partner Andrew and their children, Betty and Henry, and is looking forward to welcoming a new addition to the family soon.
Kate Morgan-Jones
Kate is one of our amazing RVN’s. She qualified from Rodbaston College in 2017 and has been working here since we opened in 2023. Her favourite part of her job is caring for our inpatients, particularly the more complex cases. She has a keen interest in monitoring anaesthetics (and giving patients a cuddle in recovery!). Outside of work, Kate and her husband have been busy building their first home. She enjoys walking her crazy Labradors and spending time outdoors!
Becca Crozier
Becca is one of our fabulous veterinary nurses! She qualified from Rodbaston College in 2020 and joined the team at Southwater just after we opened in 2023. At work, she enjoys inpatient care and supporting local rescues. A few times a month, she volunteers for StreetVet, providing veterinary care and treatment for homeless people with animals. Outside of work, she enjoys spending time with her son and pets; Bailey the cocker spaniel, Ted the cat, and 6 guinea pigs!
Charlotte Griffiths
Charlotte in another of our lovely veterinary nurses. She graduated from university in 2023 and joined the Southwater Team in 2025. Charlotte grew up on a farm, so has always had a keen interest in animals of all shapes and sizes! She has a special interest in assisting in orthopaedic and soft tissue surgeries. Outside of work, she enjoys playing hockey for her local club, running, and helping on the family farm. She has three dogs; Mick the working Border Collie, and two Jack Rusell Terriers, Pickle and Pepper.
Paige Moneypenny
Paige is one of our newest Veterinary Nurses, having only joined us in April 2026. She qualified from Myerscough University College in 2020 and is in the process of completing an Advanced Veterinary Nursing qualification. She enjoys oncology, consulting, and inpatient care. Outside of work, she is kept busy with her pets; Harvey the yellow Labrador, River the tortoiseshell cat, and Apollo the tabby cat!
Megan Willis
Megan is one of our lovely Veterinary Nurses, having only joined us in March 2026. She graduated from Myerscough University College in 2019 and has since completed a BVNA Oral Care Certificate. She enjoys all aspects of oral care – especially procedures. Outside of work, she enjoys paddleboarding, baking, and hiking with her two lovely dogs – Cody the Patterdale Cross and Jove the Miniature Schnauzer!
Debbie Goodyear
Debbie started nursing after she left school and qualified in 2003 after taking time out to go travelling. Her main hobbies include mountain biking and mountain climbing. She also goes skiing, paddleboarding, and scuba diving when she gets the chance. She has a Fox red Labrador, called Maggie, who can often be found up a mountain with her!
Student Veterinary Nurses:
Marni Perrins
Marni is one of our student Vet Nurses and started at Southwater in 2025. She is in her second year of nursing at Rodbaston College and has previously completed an ANA apprenticeship and nursing assistant qualification. Her interests at work are exotics and small mammals, theatre, and emergency care. Outside of work, she enjoys walking her dogs, camping, and reading. She has three guinea pigs, two dogs, Buddy and Rudi, and two cats, Winnie and Mavis.
Gracie Hesbrook-Hafford
Gracie started at Southwater on work experience in 2024 and has since worked her way up to studying Veterinary Nursing! She would love to specialise when she qualifies, though is still finding her niche. Outside of work, she enjoys going to the gym, seeing friends and family, and going to festivals and concerts. She has rescued 4 cats; 2 tuxedo boys, Dewey and Toby Lerone, and 2 British Shorthair girls, Lexi-Belle and Lola-Blue.
Veterinary Care Assistants:
Beth Sips
Beth is one of our amazing PCA’s, having been part of the team since June 2025. She was a dog warden for two and a half years, before completing an ANA course in 2024, and moving into her current role. She particularly enjoys surgery and looking after all of our lovely inpatients. Outside of work, she enjoys reading, gardening, and walking her two dogs; Lyra the Golden Retriever and Reiver the Labrador.
Roann Tracey
Roann is one of our fabulous PCA’s, spending most her time behind the scenes keeping everything running smoothly and caring for our inpatients. She has a degree in Animal Behaviour from the University of Chester and a master's in research. Before coming to Southwater in March 2026, she worked for the RSPCA for 2 years. Outside of work, she enjoys running, kickboxing, and walking her Pembroke Corgi, Cheddar!
Reception and administration:
Michelle Jones
Michelle came to work at Southwater when we first opened. She qualified as an RVN in 2014, after spending many years in the Royal Air Force. She now spends her time on reception.  She enjoys all aspects of working with our lovely clients. Outside of work, she is kept busy with her rescue animals – 2 horses, 3 dogs, 2 cats, and 5 chickens…not forgetting her rescue husband too!
Mel Cox
Mel has been working in the Veterinary industry for 19 years and started here at SW on Valentine’s Day 2025! At work, she enjoys talking to clients and supporting them through the journey with their pets. Outside of work, she enjoys paddleboarding, kayaking, herbalism, and spending time with her family. She has a ragdoll cat, Dexter, and a leopard gecko, called Deluca!
Neve Davis
Neve has been working at Southwater since the summer of 2025, however, has been surrounded by the veterinary environment since a very young age. She enjoys meeting all of your lovely pets, especially the spaniels! She has an ever-growing house of pets; dogs, cats, tortoises, guinea pigs, and horses! Lots of her time is spent walking and training her dogs and exercising her horses.
Sarah Caddick
Sarah is our administrator who processes the insurance claims.  With a National Diploma in Animal Management and a Higher National Diploma (HND) in Business, Sarah brings a varied background to the industry. Having joined Southwater in June 2026, she also brings over five years of industry experience to the team.
Outside of work, she enjoys taking on house renovation projects and exploring both new and familiar places. Most of all, she loves spending time with her dog, Daisy, who is her little shadow and best friend who keeps life interesting!
Debbie Baxter
Debbie has been working at Southwater since June 2025. She attended Charlton School for her GCSE’s and started working soon after. She worked in pharmacy for 24 years, before deciding on a career change. She enjoys spending time with her children and making things out of resin.
Management:
Caroline Rigby
Caroline is our operations manager and an RVN with over 30 years in the veterinary profession. Throughout her career she has worked across a wide range of clinical and leadership roles giving her a comprehensive understanding of both patient care and practice operations. Outside of work, Caroline enjoys keeping active through running, gym work, and horse riding. She also has 2 dogs, called Maxi and Minnie!
Rachel Harvey
Rachel has been Southwater’s practice manager since 2024. In 1997, she graduated from Worcester University with a degree in Sports Science. She worked in Leisure Management for 25 years, before moving to Veterinary Practice Management in 2019. Outside of work she enjoys all things fitness and spending time with her Biewer Terrier, Finn.
Emma Hughes:
Emma is our Project Manager and brings 19 years of experience within the veterinary industry. Having been part of Southwater for several years, she plays an important role in supporting the team and helping to drive projects forward.
Emma’s love for animals extends beyond the workplace too. Her family rescued Winston, a Fox Red Labrador who originally came into the practice as a stray, and he is now a much-loved member of their family.
Outside of work, Emma enjoys spending time with her two young children, walking Winston, and playing golf.
Our Practice
At Southwater Veterinary Group, we are dedicated to providing top-quality independent veterinary care for your beloved pets. Our experienced team of compassionate professionals is here to offer a wide range of services, from essential first opinion care to advanced veterinary treatments.
One of the key aspects that sets us apart is our unwavering dedication to surgical excellence. Our practice boasts a team of highly experienced veterinarians with a special interest in surgery and oncology.
We understand that prevention is key to a healthy, happy pet, which is why we offer essential services such as vaccinations, neutering, and routine check-ups.
Whether you have a new puppy or kitten, or your pet simply needs their regular health check, our skilled veterinarians are here to provide the care and guidance your pet deserves.
We understand that surgery can be a daunting prospect, and we aim to alleviate your concerns by providing meticulous pre-operative evaluations, clear communication, and compassionate post-operative care. From routine procedures to complex surgeries, we prioritise the safety and well-being of your pet at every stage.
To ensure the highest level of diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning, we have invested in cutting-edge technology. Our onsite CT scanner is a testament to our commitment to advanced veterinary care. This state-of-the-art equipment allows us to obtain detailed three-dimensional images of your pet’s internal structures, aiding in the diagnosis and treatment of a wide range of conditions. With our CT scanner, we can accurately visualise complex anatomical features, identify abnormalities, and plan surgical procedures with precision.
The practice also has extensive endoscopy and laparoscopy equipment that allows to offer options to treat conditions without aggressive open surgery, allowing quicker, less painful recoveries for things such as neutering and biopsies.
